message.content:
Here’s a mix of classic, modern, and niche horror films that have earned a reputation for being genuinely scary or unsettling:

| # | Title | Year | Why it’s worth watching |
|---|-------|------|------------------------|
| 1 | **The Shining** | 1980 | Stanley Kubrick’s masterful psychological terror set in an isolated hotel. |
| 2 | **Hereditary** | 2018 | A chilling family drama that turns into a nightmare of supernatural dread. |
| 3 | **The Exorcist** | 1973 | The quintessential demon‑possession film that still feels fresh. |
| 4 | **Get Out** | 2017 | A smart blend of horror and social commentary that keeps you on edge. |
| 5 | **A Quiet Place** | 2018 | Silence is survival; the tension is palpable. |
| 6 | **Midsommar** | 2019 | A daylight horror that turns a festival into a nightmare. |
| 7 | **It Follows** | 2014 | A modern, slow‑burn creepiness that’s all about the inevitability of the threat. |
| 8 | **The Babadook** | 2014 | Psychological horror that explores grief and motherhood. |
| 9 | **The Ring** (Japanese original) | 1998 | A haunting cursed videotape that still terrifies. |
|10 | **The Conjuring** | 2013 | A grounded supernatural thriller based on real‑life investigators. |
|11 | **Paranormal Activity** | 2007 | Found‑footage realism that makes the supernatural feel immediate. |
|12 | **The Witch** | 2015 | A slow‑burn, atmospheric horror set in 1630s New England. |
|13 | **Suspiria** (2018) | 2018 | A visually striking remake that amps up the dread. |
|14 | **The Cabin in the Woods** | 2012 | A meta‑take that subverts horror tropes while still delivering scares. |
|15 | **The Others** | 2001 | A gothic psychological thriller with a twist that will keep you guessing. |

Feel free to pick any that match your taste—whether you prefer supernatural chills, psychological dread, or a bit of both!
